terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Manual single-view camera estimate aligned to the card's long axis and three-quarter top/side view; overlay review remains the acceptance authority.

objectClass.notes: Observed as a low rectangular GPU in three-quarter view. A silver die-cast X/hourglass frame bridges two rounded black thermal panels around a narrow center waist. The implementation is an honest browser-real-time approximation of the visible view; hidden underside and internal geometry are not claimed as exact.

reasoning: The outer silhouette is simple at distance but interrupted by four diagonal frame arms, two rounded thermal apertures, and a narrow center waist.
The visible design needs separate shell, frame, thermal, bridge, rail, connector, marking, fastener, and fin systems so it can assemble in stages.
Dense diagonal fins and repeated edge hardware create high repetition density even though the macro form stays compact.
The single three-quarter reference hides the rear face, I/O bracket, PCB topology, and exact fan cavities, so those regions remain approximate.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex is justified by the layered frame and thermal hierarchy, dense repeated fins, multiple metallic responses, and detachable assembly requirement.

detailInventory.note: Nine-zone inspection of the supplied official-style product hero. Black and green background waves are excluded from object geometry.

details.description: Bright rounded metallic rim around the upper thermal panel.
Dense diagonal parallel fins inside the upper thermal aperture.
Low-roughness silver highlight along the upper frame edge.
Deep horizontal vent/recess through the center waist.
Dark rectangular power/connector cavity beside the waist vent.
Small white RTX 5090 identifier on the center bridge.
Bright rounded metallic rim around the lower-right thermal panel.
Dense diagonal parallel fins inside the lower-right thermal aperture.
Four raised metallic arms form the distinctive X/hourglass bridge.
Dark construction seam separates the X frame from both thermal panels.
GEFORCE RTX side wordmark reads as a bright white luminous strip.
Center bridge is darker and slightly more matte than the bright outer frame edges.
Continuous narrow chamfer catches light along exposed die-cast frame edges.
Tiny dark fastener accents repeat along the frame-panel perimeter.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At the reference three-quarter view, the model must immediately read as an RTX 5090 Founders Edition rather than a generic triple-fan card.
The browser model must preserve the low dual-slot proportion, two rounded thermal fields, silver X/hourglass frame, center waist, fin density, and two visible wordmarks.
Every assembly group must move from an exploded offset into a gap-free socketed final position during scroll and remain individually pickable.
Brushed metallic highlights, matte black thermal masses, edge seams, repeated fins, and luminous side marking must remain legible under neutral and grazing light.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Overall ratio follows the official 304 mm by 137 mm dual-slot envelope.
Four diagonal frame arms pinch toward the center waist and leave two rounded thermal apertures.
No triple-fan rectangle or oversized shroud replaces the Founders Edition silhouette.
failureModes: model reads as a generic add-in-board card
frame loses the X/hourglass negative space
card becomes too thick or too tall

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Backplate, thermal blocks, fin beds, frame arms, bridge, side rail, connector, bracket, and markings exist as named parts.
Thermal panels sit behind the frame and both meet the center bridge without visible gaps.
Macro, meso, and micro levels are all represented in the component hierarchy.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every detachable assembly group defines parent socket, local start/end, overlap, and gap tolerance.
Final scroll positions embed frame arms, thermal modules, bridge, rail, and bracket into the backplate by at least 0.02 object units.
Exploded offsets originate from each final local socket so parts cannot drift or snap through the core.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Silver frame uses metallic response with directional brushing and a brighter low-roughness edge override.
Thermal panels and fins use separate near-black values and roughness so the fin relief remains readable.
Center bridge is darker and more matte than the exposed frame edges.
No albedo image is reused as roughness, normal, height, or ambient occlusion.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Reference-matched view uses a cool key, soft fill, cyan rim, ACES tone mapping, dark background, and contact shadow.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and two orbit renders prove the silhouette and metallic relief independently of the supplied image.
Reference-derived color decisions are procedural and explicitly limited because the hero source contains baked lighting and green environmental reflections.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
silver frame and black thermal fields collapse into one value
lighting is evenly ambient and hides chamfers or fin relief

featureGroups.name: Founders Edition identity details
qualityCriteria: Both dense diagonal fin fields, the center vent, power cavity, RTX 5090 decal, GEFORCE RTX luminous mark, panel seams, chamfers, and perimeter fasteners are represented.
At least fourteen inventoried details map to component local features or material local overrides.
failureModes: recognizable micro details are replaced by generic noise
inventoried details exist only in prose

featureGroups.name: Interactive scroll assembly
qualityCriteria: The section remains sticky until the full card is assembled, then releases normal document scroll.
Assembly progress is deterministic from section scroll distance and has a complete reduced-motion fallback.
The final assembled card can orbit subtly, spin its fans, and highlight a clicked group without layout jank.
failureModes: continuous React state updates cause visible stutter

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence

stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Hidden underside and rear geometry use a restrained dark backplate and are intentionally approximate.
Internal PCB, vapor chamber, and fan cavities are simplified browser-real-time layers because the single hero view does not expose them.
The display bracket and port cutouts are recognizable silhouettes, not manufacturing drawings.
RTX 5090 and GEFORCE RTX labels use approximate browser decals; no exact typeface fidelity is claimed.
